title: Eighteen Months and One Empty Shelf
subtitle: 供求与需求 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 供求与需求（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与供求）
meta: 主题语境：供求与需求（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与供求）　|　核心词汇：demand　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 demand 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the buyer ① met a demand that no supplier in the town would have quoted, and she said the meeting was the whole of the season. The ② demand, meaning the wanting and not the order, ran eighteen months and stayed unlisted in the book; a demand, she said, is the only thing in a market that is judged by how long it is left unpriced.

Every ③ demand in that shop had the same empty shelf under it, and the ④ demand at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever repeated twice. A demand, her assistant said, is nine parts waiting and one part somebody willing to meet; the buyer said the waiting is the part that fills eighteen months.

The manufacturer meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the demand was the whole of the contract, meaning the order and not the wanting. The ⑥ demand, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a contract that everybody signs and nobody delivers; demand, he said, is either something you meet or the only word that means both a wanting and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ demand had become a line in an invoice, and the invoice had become an argument about the empty shelf. The ⑧ demand of the whole thing, the buyer wrote in May, was one shop and eighteen months of waiting; demand, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ demand I remember is the one at the end, which was met in 1978 and is still described as the strangest in the shop. A ⑩ demand, the assistant said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being met; every demand, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a wanting. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 需求；需要（指店里出现的那一项）
B. n. 需求（指那种想要本身，与那份订单相对）
C. 固定搭配：meet a demand 满足一项需求
D. n. 需求（指留到冬天才去满足的那一项）
E. n. 需求；求购（抽象总称，指一家店铺的全部求购）
F. n. 需求（指发票上写到、被列明的那一项）
G. n. 订单；需求量（指合同里约定的那批货）
H. n. 订单（抽象总称，指人人签字却无人交付的那一份）

items.q: met a demand that no supplier in the town would have quoted
The demand, meaning the wanting and not the order
the demand was the whole of the contract
the demand had become a line in an invoice
The demand of the whole thing
A demand, the assistant said in 1980

answers.why: meet a demand 意为“满足一项需求”，1956 年采购员满足了一项全镇没有一家供应商肯报价的需求。
demand 意为“需求”，指那种想要本身而不是那份订单，它在账簿里挂了十八个月而没有标价。
demand 意为“需求”，指那家店里每一项需求，每一项下面都是同一排空货架。
demand 意为“需求”，指留到冬天才去满足的那一项，是唯一有人重复提过两次的。
demand 意为“订单、需求量”，指合同里约定的那批货，制造商说这批货就是那份合同的全部。
demand 意为“订单”，指人人签字却无人交付的那一份而不是那种想要，是合同里人人都签字、却无人交付的东西。
demand 意为“需求”，指发票上写到、被列明的那一项，到 1963 年这项需求成了发票里的一行。
demand 意为“需求、求购”，采购员五月写道，整件事的求购是一家店铺和十八个月的等待。
demand 意为“需求”，我记得的是末尾那一项，1978 年被满足，至今仍被说成店里最奇的一项。
demand 为抽象总称，助手 1980 年说，一项需求是唯一会因为被满足而变得更好的东西。
